nodes.summary: For every predicate $p$ on a type $\alpha$ and every list $L$ over $\alpha$, linear search for $p$ on $L$ returns no index if and only if $p(x)$ is false for every element $x$ of $L$.
nodes.title: Linear search fails exactly when no element satisfies the predicate

nodes.summary: For every predicate $p$ on a type $\alpha$, every list $L = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ over $\alpha$ and every natural number $i$, linear search for $p$ on $L$ returns the index $i$ if and only if $i < n$, $p(x_i)$ is true, and $p(x_j)$ is false for every $j < i$.
nodes.title: Characterization of a successful linear search

nodes.summary: For every predicate $p$ on a type $\alpha$, every $x \in \alpha$ and every list $T$ over $\alpha$, the cost of linear search for $p$ on the list with head $x$ and tail $T$ is $1$ if $p(x)$ is true, and $1$ plus the cost of linear search for $p$ on $T$ if $p(x)$ is false. The head costs one evaluation of $p$, and the tail is searched only when the head fails.
nodes.title: Cost recurrence for linear search

nodes.summary: For every predicate $p$ on a type $\alpha$ and every list $L$ over $\alpha$, if linear search for $p$ on $L$ returns no index, then its cost is the length of $L$: it evaluates $p$ once for every element of $L$.
nodes.title: Cost of an unsuccessful linear search

nodes.summary: For every predicate $p$ on a type $\alpha$, every list $L$ over $\alpha$ and every natural number $i$, if linear search for $p$ on $L$ returns the index $i$, then its cost is $i + 1$: it evaluates $p$ exactly $i + 1$ times.
nodes.title: Cost of a successful linear search

nodes.summary: For every predicate $p$ on a type $\alpha$ and every list $L$ over $\alpha$, the cost of linear search for $p$ on $L$ is at most the length of $L$: it evaluates $p$ at most once for every element of $L$.
nodes.title: Linear search costs at most the list length

nodes.summary: For every predicate $p$ on a type $\alpha$, linear search for $p$ on the empty list has cost $0$: it evaluates $p$ zero times.
nodes.title: Cost of linear search on the empty list

nodes.summary: Given a predicate $p$ on a type $\alpha$ and a list $L$ of elements of $\alpha$, linear search scans $L$ from the front and returns the index of the first element of $L$ that satisfies $p$, or no index if no element does, together with a cost that counts one unit for each evaluation of $p$. nodes.title: Linear search

nodes.summary: For every predicate $p$ on a type $\alpha$ and every list $L = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ over $\alpha$, the index returned by linear search for $p$ on $L$ (ignoring its cost) equals the result of the standard library's first-index search: the least $i < n$ with $p(x_i)$ true, or no index if $p(x_i)$ is false for every $i < n$.
nodes.title: Linear search returns the first satisfying index

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
